hypotheses.statement: the linear trend in annual mean T2M is positive, on the order of +0.3 to +0.5 °C/decade (prior from regional literature; the estimate itself is data-driven).

models with an explicit trend or level adjustment beat seasonal naive on RMSE at long horizons mainly because seasonal naive carries one year of noise; averaging over many years in the seasonal component reduces variance. Gains are modest (MASE about 0.75 to 0.95).
ETS and SARIMA with unconstrained adaptive level will not clearly beat the harmonic regression; DM tests will often be insignificant for pairs among the non-naive models.

ceiling_check.reason: The draft is already complete and internally coherent: the forecast setup was frozen before estimation (train 1981-2022, 36-month hold-out 2023-2025), all declared models are reported against the seasonal naive and naive baselines, and the results cover trend, seasonal trends, amplitude and phase, Diebold-Mariano tests and interval calibration. The remaining gaps are the short hold-out, which limits power, and the grid-cell rather than station nature of the data. Targeted work cannot fix either of these, because the hold-out is frozen and the data are fixed. Further drafting on iteration 1 would give less than 5% qualitative improvement, and the review panel (technical, literature, writing, data, methods, plausibility) is better placed to find residual issues, such as checking the reported ~30 percent RMSE reduction against estimation_results.json and the rolling-origin evidence behind the claims.

workflow.text: Researcher decisions at the design review: the forecast setup in forecast_design.json (training 1981-01 to 2022-12, hold-out 2023-01 to 2025-12, seasonal naive and naive baselines, ETS(A,N,A), ETS(A,Ad,A), SARIMA, harmonic trend) is the design; the forecast beyond the data covers 2026-01 to 2028-12. Drop the optional ML model and the DWD station comparison (no DWD data are loaded in this study); name the station comparison as future work only. The data end in 2025-12 because the POWER monthly load covers whole years; say so. Report every declared model, including those that lose to the seasonal naive baseline.
